footprint_compatibility.profileRationale: The portal, tower and roof are one low-rise landmark composition. Mild scaling preserves it; oversized parcels repeat complete stucco window bays through the family stack.

facade_sheet.goalpost_policy: The catalogue card fixes occupied levels, roof/threshold silhouette, opening scale, construction hierarchy and material identity.

bay_strategy.rule: The whole detached house remains fixed in-band. Larger parcels repeat complete residential bays in the family-shaped fallback.

delivery.near_usage: registered skin plus physical windows, threshold, balconies, eaves, roof construction and occupied room depth

assembly_contract.side_elevations: Floor datums, material transitions, sash scale, eave and roof logic wrap every elevation; the ceremonial entrance stays fixed.

elevation_coverage.front: A three-level aged-stucco Spanish Colonial villa is anchored by a deep central stone portal and asymmetrical left bell tower, with barred recessed sash, wrought-iron balconies, exposed brick patches and a low weathered terracotta roof.
elevation_coverage.left: related occupied residential return with true sash depth
elevation_coverage.right: related occupied residential return with true sash depth

assembly_contract.variation_policy: Mild X/Y scaling keeps the whole house. Larger or distorted drawings use the family-shaped modular streetwall fallback.

reference_registration.uv_strategy: camera-registered public elevation, true-scale material zones on physical construction, occupied-depth underlay immediately behind registered glazing, and related secondary-elevation schedules wrapped around the complete envelope

material_budget.rationale: Registered facade, construction materials, physical glazing, occupied depth and small identity accents remain semantic.

architectural_identity: A three-level aged-stucco Spanish Colonial villa is anchored by a deep central stone portal and asymmetrical left bell tower, with barred recessed sash, wrought-iron balconies, exposed brick patches and a low weathered terracotta roof.
material_zones: warm hand-trowelled lime stucco; localized historic red-clay brick; pale warm limestone; dark timber sash and entrance doors; black forged iron grilles and balconies; weathered terracotta barrel tile; aged bronze bell

source_provenance.reference_method: hard catalogue goalpost, rectified registered elevation, physical residential openings and construction, occupied-depth underlay, and finite street/oblique/aerial comparison
